current_games.title: Warhammer: Vermintide 2
current_games.why: The melee-heavy ancestor of Space Marine 2's Operations mode, with rat tides that swarm exactly like Tyranids.

current_games.title: Warhammer 40,000: Darktide
current_games.why: Same 40K setting as Space Marine 2 but built around four-player gunplay and stamina-managed melee against endless poxwalker hordes.

current_games.title: Earth Defense Force 5
current_games.why: Giant-bug slaughter with absurd weapon counts — the cheerfully dumb cousin of Helldivers 2's Terminid fronts and Serious Sam's screen-filling mobs.

current_games.title: Starship Troopers: Extermination
current_games.why: Sixteen-player bug hunts with base building and hot extractions; it shares Helldivers 2's satirical military-propaganda DNA at the source.

current_games.title: Hunt: Showdown 1896
current_games.why: The most atmospheric extraction shooter going — bag the bounty, then survive the run to the exit like a tense DRG mission with other players hunting you.

current_games.title: ZERO Sievert
current_games.why: A top-down pixel-art take on Tarkov-style raids; great if you like the loot-and-escape loop but want it single-player and low-pressure.

current_games.title: The Forever Winter
current_games.why: You're a scavenger, not a supersoldier, in a war between giant machines — a grim inversion of the Space Marine 2 power fantasy with extraction rules.

current_games.title: Marauders
current_games.why: Board derelict ships, loot them, and fly out before rivals catch you — extraction raiding with the ship-boarding thrill of Sea of Thieves.

current_games.title: Post Void
current_games.why: Like ULTRAKILL, it's a hyper-kinetic, style-obsessed shooter where constant aggression is the only way to survive, and its short run-based loop echoes the speedrun chase of Neon White.

current_games.title: Severed Steel
current_games.why: Wall-running, slow-mo dives and fully destructible walls — Titanfall 2's pilot movement distilled into short, restartable arenas.

current_games.title: CULTIC
current_games.why: A broader take than Ghostrunner's parkour-slasher: retro boomer-shooter combat with slides, dodges and gory kinetic gunplay that fits your Serious Sam and ULTRAKILL streak.

current_games.title: DOOM Eternal
current_games.why: Constant dash-and-grapple movement while a Serious Sam-sized horde chases you, with the weapon-swap puzzle layered on top.

current_games.title: Batman: Arkham City
current_games.why: The freeflow combat and gliding traversal Insomniac built Spider-Man on, from the same studio behind Batman: Arkham VR.

current_games.title: Sunset Overdrive
current_games.why: Insomniac's grind-rail traversal sandbox before Spider-Man, with a wisecracking tone very close to Guardians of the Galaxy.

current_games.title: Enslaved: Odyssey to the West
current_games.why: Since Fallen Order's punishing soulslike combat didn't land, this swaps in breezy, momentum-driven traversal and a character-led story much closer to Uncharted and Guardians of the Galaxy. Its colorful post-apocalyptic vistas and buddy-banter script carry the cinematic weight instead of difficulty.

current_games.title: Prince of Persia: The Sands of Time
current_games.why: The older blueprint for Uncharted and Tomb Raider — wall-runs, collapsing ruins and a charming narrator, all in about eight hours.

current_games.title: Astroneer
current_games.why: Terrain-deforming planetary mining with friends — Deep Rock Galactic's digging and Trailmakers' build-a-rover tinkering in one relaxed package.

current_games.title: Barotrauma
current_games.why: Crewing a submarine under Europa's ice is Subnautica's deep-sea dread crossed with the crisis-management chaos of a bad Deep Rock run.

current_games.title: Lethal Company
current_games.why: Scrap quotas, a departure deadline and terrible voice comms — a tiny indie distillation of the DRG mission loop with extraction-shooter nerves.

current_games.title: Grounded
current_games.why: Backyard survival with base building and genuinely scary bugs; it hits the Subnautica progression rhythm with four-player co-op built in.

current_games.title: Project Wingman
current_games.why: A three-person indie love letter to Ace Combat, missile spam, cheesy radio chatter and all — plus a full VR mode.

current_games.title: Crimson Skies: High Road to Revenge
current_games.why: Where Squadrons chased cockpit-sim realism, this is pure pulp arcade flying — zeppelin raids, barnstorming stunts and a swashbuckling story that scratches the same Ace Combat itch with a Sea of Thieves-style pirate swagger.

current_games.title: House of the Dying Sun
current_games.why: A short, brutal space-fighter game about commanding a strike wing; pure arcade precision for Ace Combat players who want it in zero-g.

current_games.title: EVERSPACE 2
current_games.why: Hand-crafted space combat with loot and exploration — the dogfighting feel of Ace Combat wrapped around a Subnautica-ish urge to poke at every wreck.
